transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I came in because my head just doesn’t stay where it’s supposed to anymore. Like at work, I’ll be doing inventory, counting supplies, and then I lose track of what I was counting. Or I’ll go to the supply closet and just stand there like, “What did I come in here for?”

And I’ve been trying to study for this supervisor certification thing—well, I’ve been meaning to, because it could help me move up—but I keep reading the same line over and over and it just doesn’t stick. It’s frustrating, because I used to be better at keeping things straight.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things you're trying to do?

Yeah, I do. That’s kind of what finally pushed me to come in. My head just doesn’t stay on task anymore. Like I’ll be doing inventory at work, and I’m supposed to be counting supplies, but then I lose where I was and have to start over.

Or I go to the supply closet and just stand there, and it’s embarrassing because sometimes someone walks by and I pretend I’m looking for something, but really I’m trying to remember why I came in there. And with the supervisor certification stuff, I’ll read the same line again and again and it’s like it won’t stick. It makes me feel… I don’t know, like my brain is just not doing its job.
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed by these difficulties with focusing and remembering things?

I’m not really sure. I mean… overwhelmed, maybe sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious. It’s more like I get frustrated and then I start thinking about how I should’ve written things down, or I’ll remember this one time I lost a whole set of keys at work and spent half the shift retracing my steps.

So, yeah, it bothers me. I don’t know exactly what you mean by anxious, though.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling frustrated, is it related to feeling worried or on edge about your situation?

I don’t know… frustrated is more like, I get annoyed with myself. Like, “Come on, why can’t you just remember the thing?” I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there on edge exactly.

It’s like when you put something down and then you’re late because you can’t find it, and suddenly you’re tearing through drawers and checking the same pocket three times. Actually, I used to have this junk drawer at home where everything ended up—batteries, receipts, old keys—and I kept telling myself I’d organize it, but then I’d just make it worse trying to find one thing.

So… worried? Maybe a little in the moment, but mostly I just feel irritated and kind of stuck. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless?

Restless… I’m not sure. I mean, I move around a lot at work because that’s the job, you know, sweeping and taking trash out and all that, so it’s hard for me to tell if that counts.

If I’m sitting somewhere, I might shift around or mess with something in my hands, but I don’t really pay attention to it. Like if I’m in the break room and there’s one of those paper coffee sleeves, I’ll fold it up without thinking, but I don’t know if that’s fidgeting or just… something to do. I guess I haven’t really noticed it as a big thing.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain tasks or activities because you're worried you'll struggle to remember things or keep track of what you're doing?

Yeah… I guess I do avoid some things, not always on purpose. Like at work, I still get the cleaning done, I’m not just leaving stuff, but I’m slower because I keep checking myself, like, did I log that room, did I miss the supply closet, did I write it down right.

And there was talk before about maybe trying for a supervisor kind of track, but I stopped pushing for that. It just feels like too much to keep track of, all the notes and people asking where things are. Even outside work, I’ve skipped neighborhood clean-ups and some family get-togethers I used to make time for, because I don’t want to show up and then feel like I’m losing the thread of what I’m supposed to be doing.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends, family, or coworkers since you started having these difficulties with focusing and remembering things?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, not like everyone suddenly hates me or anything, but I’ve pulled back some.

At work I still do the cleaning, but I’m slower, and I keep second-guessing my logs—like whether I wrote down the right room or checked the right thing. And then if someone asks me something later, I feel embarrassed, like I should know. There was even talk before about maybe moving toward a supervisor kind of thing, but I kind of stopped pushing for it. It just feels like too much to keep straight.

With family and other people… I’ve skipped some get-togethers, and those neighborhood clean-up things I used to go to. Which is kind of funny because I already clean all day, so you’d think I’d avoid cleaning on purpose, but I used to like those because you’d see people, talk a little. Now I just think, what if I forget what I’m supposed to be doing or lose track, and then I just don’t go. So yeah, I guess it’s made me more distant.
Do you ever feel sad or down when you're not able to remember things or stay focused?

Yeah… I do. I mean, it’s not only when I forget something, but that definitely makes it worse.

Most days it feels like there’s this heavy, flat feeling kind of following me around. Like I’ll be pushing the cleaning cart down an empty hallway, and it’s quiet except the wheels squeaking, and I’ll just feel… low. Or I’ll be sitting with my family trying to act normal, listening to whatever they’re talking about, and I’m there, but I don’t really feel there.

And then if I can’t remember something or I lose focus, it sort of proves what I was already feeling, if that makes sense. Like, there it is again. So yeah, sad, down… kind of worn out by it.
Have you always had trouble focusing and remembering things, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

No, I don’t think it was always like this. I mean, I was never perfect with paperwork or anything, but this got noticeable maybe… about three years ago.

That was around when the contractor switched us to rotating evening and overnight shifts, especially at the bigger properties. Those places are harder to keep straight anyway—different floors, different closets, people leaving notes in weird spots. And, uh, I remember thinking at first it was just because the schedule was throwing me off. Like when you’re leaving work and the sun’s coming up, it makes the whole day feel backwards.

But yeah… about three years. That’s when it really started feeling like I couldn’t keep track the same way.
Have you had to make significant changes to your daily routine because of these memory and focus issues?

Yeah, I guess I have. Not like I made some big written schedule or anything, but I’ve changed what I take on.

I still get the cleaning done, you know, I’m not just leaving things unfinished, but I move slower now because I keep checking myself. Like I’ll write something in the log and then stare at it, wondering if I put the right room down or if I already did that area. It eats up time.

And there was this whole thing where I might’ve tried to move toward a supervisor spot, or at least that was kind of mentioned before, but I’ve stopped pushing for that. Too many details to keep track of, too many chances to mess something up.

Outside work, too… I don’t go to the neighborhood clean-ups much anymore, even though I used to like seeing people there. And family stuff, I skip more than I used to. I’ll tell myself I’m tired or busy, but really it’s partly because I don’t want to lose track of things or feel embarrassed. So yeah, my routine’s gotten smaller, I guess.
Have you noticed that these difficulties with focusing and remembering things have significantly impacted your ability to perform your job or maintain relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still doing the job. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just not showing up or leaving trash sitting there, because I do get it done.

But it’s definitely affected it. I’m slower now because I keep checking myself, especially the logs. I’ll write something down and then keep looking back like, wait, did I put the right room, did I already do that floor, did I miss a note from somebody. It’s like I don’t trust my own head.

And, uh… there was a point where people kind of talked like maybe I could move toward supervisor stuff, but I don’t really push for that anymore. Too many things to track, and I don’t want to be the guy who messes it up.

Relationships, too, I guess. Not in some big dramatic way, but I skip more things now. Neighborhood clean-ups, family get-togethers… stuff I used to make time for. Sometimes I say I’m tired, which is true enough, but part of it is I just don’t want to be there and lose track of something or feel stupid in front of people.
Do you experience these difficulties with focusing and remembering things every day?

Pretty much every day, yeah. Some days it’s not as bad, but it’s there.

Like I’ll be doing inventory and I’ll walk to the supply closet and then just stand there thinking, wait, what did I come in here for? Or I’ll try to study for that supervisor certification thing, and I keep reading the same line over and over, and it just doesn’t stick. Then I get annoyed and start straightening papers or checking my phone or thinking about some random thing, like whether we’re low on floor pads, and then I’ve lost another half hour.

So… yeah. It’s not every single minute, but it comes up most days.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about your situation?

Yeah… I do. Maybe not like I’m sitting there saying “I’m worthless” all day, but it kind of comes out that way in my head.

I’ll think, you know, other guys my age would’ve figured this out by now. They’d adjust, move up, take on more. And I’m still over here trying not to miss small things at work, like checking the same notes again or worrying I messed up some little detail.

It makes me feel like… maybe I’m just not cut out for more than this. And then I feel bad even saying that, because the job matters, it’s honest work. My uncle used to do maintenance at a school, actually, and he was proud of it—he had this whole thing about keeping floors looking good—but, I don’t know, for me it turns into this thing where I feel like I should be doing better by now.
Have you ever felt so down that you thought you'd be better off dead?

I… I don’t know. I mean, I get really low sometimes, but “better off dead” is a big thing to say.

Sometimes I think more like… I wish I could just not have to deal with everything for a while, you know? Like when the trash compactor jams and then the whole loading area smells bad and everyone’s acting like it’s your fault, even though it’s usually somebody putting cardboard in wrong—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I’m not sure how to answer it. I’ve felt pretty down, but I don’t know if I’d put it exactly that way.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days for the past two weeks?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s not always like I’m crying or anything obvious like that, but there’s this heavy, flat feeling that kind of follows me around.

Like I’ll be pushing the cart down an empty hallway at work, and everything’s quiet except the wheels squeaking—actually one of them’s been messed up for weeks, I keep meaning to ask about replacing it—and I’ll just feel… low. Or I’m at home with my family, sitting there trying to act normal, and it’s still there in the background.

So, yeah. For the past couple weeks, most days.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

I’m not sure… I mean, I still do some things, but I don’t know if I enjoy them the same or if I’m just doing them out of habit.

Like sometimes I’ll put on a game or try to watch something, and then I realize I’ve been looking at my phone half the time anyway. But then again, maybe everybody does that now. My cousin can’t watch anything without scrolling, and he says that’s normal, so I don’t know.

I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s “lost interest” exactly. It’s more like… things don’t always grab me the way they used to, but I don’t know how much of that counts.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, flat feeling that you described?

Probably… about three years now, if I’m being honest.

It kind of started after the contractor changed our schedule to those rotating evening and overnight shifts, especially at the bigger properties. Before that it wasn’t like everything was great, but I don’t remember having this same flat feeling all the time.

The overnight stuff really messes with everything—like one week you’re cleaning offices after everyone leaves, then another you’re at some huge place where the lights are half off and it’s just you and the floor buffer making that awful hum. Sorry, I’m getting off track. But yeah… around three years. Since that change.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you didn't feel sad or down at all?

Not really, no. I mean, maybe there are moments where I’m distracted and I’m not thinking about it, like if I’m focused on getting something done, but I wouldn’t say there’s been a whole day where it’s just gone.

Most days it’s that same heavy, flat feeling kind of following me around. Even when I’m just pushing the cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting with my family trying to act normal, it’s still kind of there in the background.
Have you had any thoughts of self-harm or suicide in the past two weeks?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches where I think, like, I’m tired of feeling this way, or I wish I could just shut everything off for a while.

But when you say self-harm or suicide, I’m not sure where the line is exactly. I haven’t really… I don’t know. It’s not something I’ve sat down and made a plan about or anything like that.

Sorry, I know that’s not a straight answer. My brain kind of jumps around with stuff like this.
Have you felt sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two years or more?

Yeah… I think so. Most days it feels like there’s this heavy, flat thing kind of following me around.

Like I’ll be doing normal stuff, pushing the cleaning cart down some empty hallway, or sitting with my family trying to act like I’m fine, and it’s still there in the background. I might get distracted for a bit, but it doesn’t really feel like it fully lifts.

I’ll think, you know, other guys my age would’ve figured this out by now. They’d adjust, move up, take on more. And I’m still over here trying not to miss small things at work, like checking the same notes again or worrying I messed up some little detail.

It makes me feel like… maybe I’m just not cut out for more than this. And then I feel bad even saying that, because the job matters, it’s honest work. My uncle used to do maintenance at a school, actually, and he was proud of it—he had this whole thing about keeping floors looking good—but, I don’t know, for me it turns into this thing where I feel like I should be doing better by now.

I… I don’t know. I mean, I get really low sometimes, but “better off dead” is a big thing to say.

Sometimes I think more like… I wish I could just not have to deal with everything for a while, you know? Like when the trash compactor jams and then the whole loading area smells bad and everyone’s acting like it’s your fault, even though it’s usually somebody putting cardboard in wrong—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I’m not sure how to answer it. I’ve felt pretty down, but I don’t know if I’d put it exactly that way.

Like I’ll be pushing the cart down an empty hallway at work, and everything’s quiet except the wheels squeaking—actually one of them’s been messed up for weeks, I keep meaning to ask about replacing it—and I’ll just feel… low. So, yeah. For the past couple weeks, most days.

I’m not sure… I mean, I still do some things, but I don’t know if I enjoy them the same or if I’m just doing them out of habit.

Like sometimes I’ll put on a game or try to watch something, and then I realize I’ve been looking at my phone half the time anyway. But then again, maybe everybody does that now. My cousin can’t watch anything without scrolling, and he says that’s normal, so I don’t know.

I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s “lost interest” exactly. It’s more like… things don’t always grab me the way they used to, but I don’t know how much of that counts.

Probably… about three years now, if I’m being honest.

It kind of started after the contractor changed our schedule to those rotating evening and overnight shifts, especially at the bigger properties. Before that it wasn’t like everything was great, but I don’t remember having this same flat feeling all the time.

The overnight stuff really messes with everything—like one week you’re cleaning offices after everyone leaves, then another you’re at some huge place where the lights are half off and it’s just you and the floor buffer making that awful hum. Sorry, I’m getting off track. But yeah… around three years. Since that change.
